title: Given a Scenario, Monitor Mobile Device Hardware and Use Appropriate Replacement Techniques

sections.title: What You Are Learning
paragraphs: Mobile devices pack many replaceable or serviceable components into a small space. For this objective, recognize the hardware responsible for a failing function and the considerations that guide a safe, compatible replacement.
The main troubleshooting pattern is: identify the failing function, locate the hardware responsible, determine whether it is actually replaceable, then perform and verify the appropriate replacement.
bullets: Physical privacy and security components, including biometrics and near-field scanner features
sections.callout: Identify the failing function → locate the responsible hardware → choose a safe, compatible replacement technique.

sections.title: Maestro Focus
paragraphs: When a mobile device has a hardware problem, can you identify the responsible internal component and what must be checked before replacing it?
bullets: Wireless radio or reception problem → Wireless card or antenna
Identity or proximity feature → Physical privacy/security hardware

sections.title: Battery
paragraphs: The battery stores portable electrical power. Short battery life, unexpected shutdowns, failure to hold a charge, or failure when disconnected from external power can indicate a battery problem.
A device that will not charge does not automatically need a battery. The charger, charging port, internal connection, or another power component may be responsible.
sections.callout: The device works on external power but loses power quickly when unplugged → suspect the battery.

sections.title: Battery Replacement
paragraphs: Battery access varies by device. Some batteries are externally accessible; others require opening the enclosure and disconnecting delicate internal cables.

Power down as appropriate, disconnect external power, follow the manufacturer's service procedure, and use a compatible replacement. Never puncture, crush, compress, or excessively bend a lithium-based battery.
bullets: Treat swelling or deformation as a physical battery-safety warning.
Do not force a swollen battery back into place.
Protect connectors and surrounding components during removal.
Verify normal charging and portable operation after replacement.
sections.callout: Swollen or deformed battery → stop normal use and follow safe battery-handling procedures.

sections.title: Keyboard and Keys
paragraphs: Laptop keyboard failures may affect one key, several keys, a region of the keyboard, or the whole assembly. Symptoms include sticking, no response, repeated characters, or inconsistent input.
A single damaged key may involve the keycap or its mechanism. Wider failure may require checking the keyboard cable, connection, or keyboard assembly.
sections.callout: One damaged physical key → inspect the key mechanism. Multiple keys or the whole keyboard fail → investigate the assembly and connection.

sections.title: Random-Access Memory (RAM)
paragraphs: Random-access memory (RAM) is temporary working memory used while the system operates. Some laptops use replaceable compact memory modules; other mobile systems integrate memory permanently into the system board.
Before replacement or upgrade, confirm that the RAM is serviceable, the supported memory type and capacity, available slots, and module compatibility.
bullets: Shut down and disconnect power as appropriate.
Release retaining clips carefully and align the replacement correctly.
Seat the module without forcing it and verify that the system recognizes it.
sections.callout: New RAM is not detected → check compatibility, alignment, and seating.

sections.title: HDD and SSD Storage
paragraphs: Hard disk drives and solid-state drives provide persistent storage for the operating system, applications, configuration, and user files. Their key difference is the technology used to store data.

table.caption: HDD and SSD recognition
rows: Magnetic media with moving mechanical components
Abnormal mechanical sounds or shock-related failure
Electronic storage with no spinning platters
Fast, compact storage without moving disk components

sections.callout: HDD spins; SSD does not. Both retain data after shutdown.

sections.title: Storage Replacement
paragraphs: Before replacing an HDD or SSD, determine the required form factor, interface, physical compatibility, capacity, and whether data must be backed up or migrated.
After installation, the system may require operating-system installation, restoration from backup, data migration, and confirmation that firmware or the operating system detects the drive.
sections.callout: Replacement storage is not detected → check physical installation, interface connection, firmware detection, and compatibility.

sections.title: Wireless Cards
paragraphs: A wireless card provides the networking radio, commonly for Wi-Fi. It may be a replaceable module or integrated into the system board.

Wireless failures can also result from antenna connections, antenna placement, configuration, drivers, or software. Do not replace the card until those possibilities have been separated from an actual card failure.
sections.callout: The card provides the radio; the antenna provides the signal path.

sections.title: Wi-Fi Antenna Connector and Placement
paragraphs: Laptop antenna wiring often runs through the chassis into the display area. Small, delicate leads connect those antennas to the wireless card.
A disconnected, loose, damaged, reversed, or poorly placed antenna lead can cause weak reception even when the wireless card works correctly.
sections.callout: Wi-Fi becomes weak after laptop service or card replacement → verify antenna connectors and placement.

entries.title: Biometrics
paragraphs: Biometric hardware uses a physical characteristic to identify or authenticate a user. Examples include fingerprint readers and supported facial-recognition hardware.
Failure may involve the physical sensor, connection, configuration, or software.
entries.recognitionCue: A fingerprint or another physical characteristic unlocks the device → biometrics.

entries.title: Near-Field Scanner Features
paragraphs: Near-field scanner features interact with compatible tags or objects at very close range. The scanner component or antenna must remain properly positioned and connected after service.
entries.memoryHook: Near-field asks: What is near me?
entries.recognitionCue: A device must be brought very close to a compatible item → near-field scanner feature.

sections.title: Camera and Webcam
paragraphs: A camera/webcam captures images and video. Mobile cameras may be integrated into a display assembly, face forward or backward, and connect through small internal cables or modules.

No image, intermittent video, physical damage, or a device-not-detected condition can indicate hardware trouble. However, privacy settings, application permissions, configuration, and drivers must also be considered.
sections.callout: The camera fails only in one application → check permissions and application settings before replacing hardware.

sections.title: Microphone
paragraphs: A microphone captures audio input for calls, meetings, recordings, and voice commands. A mobile device may have one or more integrated microphones.
No sound, low input, distortion, or intermittent input may be caused by hardware, but also check permissions, input selection, application settings, physical obstruction, and internal connections.
sections.callout: The user hears others, but nobody hears the user → investigate the microphone and audio-input path.

sections.title: Camera vs. Microphone

table.caption: Video-conference input symptoms
rows: Others can hear the user but cannot see the user
Others can see the user but cannot hear the user

sections.callout: No picture does not automatically mean a bad camera, and no sound does not automatically mean a bad microphone—rule out permissions and configuration first.

sections.title: Appropriate Mobile Hardware Replacement
paragraphs: Mobile devices are tightly packed and often use delicate cables, clips, connectors, and integrated assemblies. Diagnose before replacing parts.
bullets: Identify the symptom and the component that could cause it.
Rule out configuration and software causes when appropriate.
Determine whether the component is serviceable or integrated.
Verify replacement compatibility and follow the manufacturer's procedure.
Power down safely and protect against electrostatic discharge.
Protect delicate connectors, cables, clips, and surrounding components.
Reassemble correctly and test the repaired function.
sections.callout: Diagnose → Replace → Verify. Troubleshooting is not a parts-swapping contest.

sections.title: Recognition Cues
bullets: Swollen internal power source → Battery safety issue
Weak Wi-Fi after internal service → Wi-Fi antenna connector/placement

sections.title: Objective 1.1 Exam Trap
paragraphs: The biggest trap is assuming that the component associated with a symptom must automatically be replaced. Match the symptom to the function, then rule out connections, permissions, configuration, compatibility, and other simpler causes.

entries.title: Battery vs. Charging Problem
paragraphs: Failure to charge can involve the battery, charger, port, connection, or another power component. Working on external power but failing when unplugged makes the battery a stronger suspect.

entries.title: RAM vs. Storage
paragraphs: RAM is temporary working memory. HDDs and SSDs provide persistent storage that remains after shutdown.

entries.title: Wireless Card vs. Antenna
paragraphs: The card is the wireless radio. The antenna is its signal path. Weak reception immediately after service points strongly toward the antenna connection or placement.

entries.title: Hardware Failure vs. Configuration
paragraphs: Camera, microphone, and wireless functions may fail even when the physical component is healthy. Check permissions, settings, drivers, and connections before replacement.

sections.callout: Match the symptom, rule out simpler causes, verify compatibility, replace safely, and test the result.

sections.title: Maestro Recognition Sheet
bullets: Persistent storage without moving disks → SSD
Weak signal after internal service → Wi-Fi antenna connector/placement
Very-close-range scanner capability → Near-field scanner feature
Memory not detected after installation → Check seating and compatibility
Replacement drive not detected → Check installation, connection, and compatibility
Mobile hardware repair → Diagnose → Replace → Verify
